data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and reviewing weak areas like Unit 9. Ensure all units are covered in the first 8 weeks.
data.summary: This 10-week plan prioritizes the weak Unit 9 in the first half, covering all other units sequentially. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to solidify understanding before the exam.

weeks.focus: Master entropy and Gibbs free energy concepts.
tasks: Do 10 free-response questions on entropy changes, then mark them against the scoring guide.
Complete a problem set on calculating Gibbs free energy for 5 reactions.
Review lecture notes on thermodynamic favorability and create a summary sheet.

weeks.focus: Understand electrochemical cells and their applications.
tasks: Build a simple galvanic cell model and label all components.
Solve 8 problems on calculating cell potential and electrolysis.
Practice identifying anode and cathode in 10 different cell diagrams.

weeks.focus: Learn atomic structure and periodic trends.
tasks: Complete a worksheet on electron configurations for 15 elements.
Practice interpreting mass spectra for 5 different elements.
Create a chart of periodic trends for ionization energy and atomic radius.
Draw Lewis structures for 10 molecules, including resonance forms.
Practice VSEPR theory by predicting shapes for 8 molecules.
Solve 5 problems on formal charge and hybridization.

weeks.focus: Explore properties of substances and mixtures.
tasks: Complete a table comparing intermolecular forces for 6 substances.
Solve 8 ideal gas law problems.
Practice kinetic molecular theory questions on particle behavior.
Balance 10 chemical equations and write net ionic equations for 5.
Solve 8 stoichiometry problems involving limiting reactants.
Practice identifying physical vs. chemical changes in 10 scenarios.

weeks.focus: Study reaction kinetics and rate laws.
tasks: Do 10 free-response questions on rate laws, then mark them against the scoring guide.
Solve 8 problems on concentration changes over time.
Practice identifying elementary reactions and rate-determining steps.
Solve 8 calorimetry problems.
Practice calculating equilibrium constants for 5 reactions.
Review energy diagrams for endothermic and exothermic processes.

weeks.focus: Mixed review of all units with timed practice.
tasks: Complete a 45-minute timed practice test covering Units 1-5.
Review incorrect answers and re-do 5 problems from Unit 9.
Practice 10 free-response questions from mixed topics.
Complete a full 90-minute timed practice exam.
Review all weak areas, especially Unit 9.
Create a final summary sheet of key formulas and concepts.
